title: Normalization of point Frobenius transport on free coefficient sheaves
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ with $q=p^a$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $g=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, where $\gamma$ is geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. For $B=A_{E,n}$ or $\mathcal O_E$, write $B_s$ for its constant or completed coefficient sheaf, respectively [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $M$ be a finite free $B_s$-module sheaf placed in degree zero whose class belongs to $D^b_c(s,B)$. Regard $g^{-1}M$ as a $B_s$-module through the coefficient structure isomorphism $c_B:g^{-1}B_s\to B_s$. Let $\kappa_M:g^{-1}M\to Lg^*M$ be the specified comparison [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], $\lambda_M:Lg^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}g^{-1}M$ the following normalized identification (an isomorphism of the type asserted in [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]): at finite level it is the sheafified multiplication map $x\otimes b\mapsto c_B^{-1}(b)x$; at integral level put $G=g^{-1}$, let $u_M:M\to\widehat M$ be the actual derived-completion unit and $\theta_{g,M}:Lg^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}G\widehat M$ the entire-cone comparison of [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization], and set $\lambda_M=G(u_M)^{-1}\circ\theta_{g,M}$, where $u_M$ is invertible by [lem-pur-normalized-actual-reconstruction-maps] since $M\in D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and $\sigma_M$ restriction along $g:(s,g)\to(s,\operatorname{id})$ followed by the inverse-image coprojection [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. Then
$$\lambda_M\circ\kappa_M=\operatorname{id}_{g^{-1}M}\quad\text{in }D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},B).$$
At finite level these inverse coordinate maps are $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ and $x\otimes b\mapsto c_B^{-1}(b)x$. For completed coefficients their reductions are these maps at every $A_{E,r}$, and the same identity holds for the specified derived inverse-limit comparison. In the Frobenius square with structural map $\operatorname{id}_s$, the ordinary direct-image exchange [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] is the identity under the identity-operation identifications. Consequently, for any $B_s$-linear sheaf isomorphism $v:g^{-1}M\to M$ and $\theta=v\circ\lambda_M$, the ordinary transport [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] satisfies
$$\Gamma(s,\theta)\circ\tau_M=\Gamma(s,v)\circ\sigma_M\quad\text{in }D(B).$$
The coefficient composite $\Gamma(s,c_B)\circ\sigma_{B_s}$ fixes each element of $B$. The maps $\sigma$ commute with the canonical tensor and dual evaluation maps, where the dual is $M^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{B_s}(M,B_s)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom], tensor is the sheafified tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and inverse-image comparisons are those of [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom]. The rational versions are the images under $-\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$, and the algebraically closed versions are represented by them at a common finite stage [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point].

proof.text: Use the finite multiplication inverse, localize its inverse identity with the specified exact-functor comparisons, and cancel kappa-lambda. Substitute the identity-exchange sigma-kappa recipe and functoriality to obtain the finite equation for every v.

Use the canonical pointQuotientComparisonData and its proved determining coordinate API, obtaining j and eta with the specified generator inverse and both cone coordinates. The generator equation and the section specification of kappa make j hom a left inverse sectionwise; the finite multiplication hom is a right inverse. Function.LeftInverse.eq_rightInverse identifies their section functions and transfers the full scalar formula. The two cone coordinates and isomorphismRoosUnitCancellation give the whole augmentation equality, with explicit categorical reassociation. Work sectionwise because the tower components have completed scalar action after restriction, whereas the finite isomorphism is over the finite coefficient ring.

Convert intrinsic completeness to the legacy predicate using an explicit universe-zero finite-field datum at a prime greater than l. Apply the whole-cone normalization theorem to a coherent evaluation calculus and retain its two-sided inverse of the fixed kappa. The complete field of the recorded Frobenius models makes the recorded actual unit an isomorphism epsilon. Define theta as inverse kappa followed by G(epsilon). The kappa inverse identity gives kappa followed by theta equals G(epsilon), and cancellation of G(epsilon) gives the integral kappa-lambda identity.
Substitute the integral identity-exchange recipe, cancel kappa-lambda, and apply the rational and common-stage scalar functors to the resulting equality for every v.

Apply point restriction normalization to the coefficient section and cancel the coefficient map with its inverse. Tensor compatibility is naturality of the module-sheafification unit on a pure tensor. Internal-Hom evaluation compatibility is naturality of the local module map on the corresponding slice arrow. Assemble the three clauses.
